promotion_policy: No candidate in this packet may be copied into a reader-eligible source, marked approved, or served until the owner explicitly approves the exact wording.
authoring_policy: Candidates are rewritten from the current lunation mechanism and house/axis meaning rather than from the legacy pending prose. Legacy review-held copy remains preserved as source history only.

candidates.body:
You may be done organizing your life around a version of yourself that other people still recognize. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 1st house, bringing a culmination around identity, appearance, agency, and the way you move through the world, while the Virgo side of the axis exposes the relationships and agreements that have helped define you. You might change how you present yourself, stop explaining a decision that has already become clear, or notice that a role you accepted in a relationship no longer fits the person you are now.

The important part is not making a dramatic reinvention out of every feeling. Eclipses can accelerate developments before you have language for all of them. Pay attention to what has become difficult to keep pretending about yourself, especially when another person's expectations are the main reason you are hesitating. You do not need a finished identity before you make the next decision. You need enough honesty to stop building around one that has already expired.

Money may be showing you which parts of your life are actually sustainable. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 2nd house, bringing a culmination around income, spending, possessions, and what your work is worth, while the Virgo side of the axis puts shared money, debt, taxes, and other people's obligations into the same calculation. An account balance, invoice, payment, contract, or recurring cost may make a financial truth harder to keep abstract.

This is not a verdict on your worth. It is information about the terms you are living with. You may need to raise a rate, cut a cost that no longer makes sense, change how a shared expense is divided, or admit that a plan requires more money than you can responsibly give it. Do not turn one number into a story about your value. Use the number to make the decision it actually belongs to. What you can rely on grows when the math and the promise finally describe the same life.

Information you have been collecting may finally change the conclusion. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 3rd house, bringing a culmination around messages, conversations, learning, paperwork, siblings, neighbors, and the information moving through your everyday life. Across the axis, Virgo in the 9th house tests the larger belief, plan, legal question, educational path, or long-range direction against the details you can now verify.

A conversation may confirm what you suspected, a document may change the plan, or a piece of information you once dismissed may become the detail that matters most. The risk is filling the gaps with a story because uncertainty is uncomfortable. Separate what you know from what you inferred, then decide what the new information actually changes. You do not need to keep defending the earlier conclusion simply because you built plans around it. Better information is allowed to produce a different answer.

Something about home or family may have reached the point where dealing with it later no longer works. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 4th house, bringing a culmination around home, family, property, living arrangements, and the private life that supports everything you do outside it. Virgo across the axis brings career, visibility, responsibility, and public demands into the same decision.

A move may become necessary, a family role may need clearer limits, a property issue may require a decision, or you may realize that your current living situation cannot keep absorbing the cost of the life you are building. This does not mean every difficult feeling needs a dramatic exit. It means the private arrangement has to work in practice. Pay attention to what happens when nobody is impressed by the title, plan, or public progress. Your home life should not have to carry every consequence of what the rest of your life requires.

A source of joy may need more time, or a situation you kept calling fun may no longer feel that way. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 5th house, bringing a culmination around creativity, romance, pleasure, children, and the things you choose because they make life feel more alive. Virgo across the axis brings friendships, groups, audiences, collaborators, and long-term goals into the picture.

You may finish or finally share a creative project, see a romantic situation more clearly, make a decision involving a child, or realize that a group expectation has been taking time from something you actually care about. The answer is not to turn every pleasure into a plan for the future. It is to notice what still gives something back to you after the attention, excitement, or social approval wears off. Give more time to the part of your life you would still choose if nobody else needed to understand why it matters.

Your schedule may finally show you what your body and workload have been trying to say. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 6th house, bringing a culmination around daily work, routines, health, appointments, coworkers, and the systems that determine how your days actually function. Virgo across the axis brings rest, recovery, private strain, and the work you have been compensating for behind the scenes into view.

A routine may stop working, an appointment may change the way you manage your time, or a responsibility you have been quietly carrying may become impossible to keep fitting around everything else. Do not confuse being able to push through something with proof that the arrangement is sustainable. Look at sleep, meals, travel time, workload, and the gaps between commitments. The useful change is the one that makes ordinary days more workable after the immediate pressure passes.

A relationship can reach a turning point before you know what its final form should be. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 7th house, bringing a culmination around partnerships, clients, contracts, commitments, and the agreements that make another person's choices consequential to your life. Virgo across the axis makes your own standards, time, body, and priorities impossible to leave out of the decision.

Someone may want a clearer commitment, a contract may need new terms, a client relationship may change, or you may realize that affection has been doing too much of the work for an arrangement that is weak on follow-through. You do not need to decide that a relationship is good or bad in order to name what is no longer working. Look at the actual agreement. What is each person responsible for, what keeps landing on you, and what happens after the apology or promise? Let the next version be built from what both people can consistently support.

Shared money or shared responsibility may need new terms. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 8th house, bringing a culmination around debt, taxes, inheritance, investments, shared accounts, intimacy, and the agreements that determine who carries what when resources are combined. Virgo across the axis brings your own income, possessions, and financial limits into the same conversation.

A payment plan may end, funding may change, an estate or tax matter may move forward, or a relationship may force a more precise conversation about access, obligation, and trust. Generosity is not a substitute for clear terms. Neither is closeness. Know what you owe, what you own, what you can access, and what someone else is expecting you to cover before another commitment is added. The emotional part matters, but clarity is what keeps shared resources from becoming shared confusion.

A belief, plan, or long-range direction may change once you have enough evidence to stop defending the old version. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 9th house, bringing a culmination around education, travel, publishing, teaching, legal matters, belief, and the larger ideas shaping where you think your life can go. Virgo across the axis pulls messages, paperwork, local facts, and ordinary conversations into the decision.

You may finish a course, change an educational plan, publish something, make a travel decision, or receive information that changes your position on a subject you thought was settled. Conviction is useful until it becomes a reason to ignore the detail that does not fit. Read the document, check the date, follow up, and let new evidence change the plan if it needs to. A larger perspective should help you understand more of what is happening, not require you to explain away the facts in front of you.

Your public role may change because you can no longer separate recognition from what the role actually costs you. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 10th house, bringing a culmination around career, reputation, leadership, visibility, and the responsibilities attached to being known for what you do. Virgo across the axis brings home, family, property, and private obligations into the same decision.

A promotion, departure, launch, leadership change, or public decision may clarify what you want to be responsible for next. The title is only part of the story. Look at the hours, authority, compensation, travel, support, and effect on your private life. More recognition should not require you to keep absorbing responsibilities that were never matched by better terms. Let the professional change become concrete enough that the life behind it can support it too.

A friendship, group, audience, or long-term goal may show you where belonging and direction have stopped matching. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 11th house, bringing a culmination around friendships, communities, professional networks, audiences, and the future plans that depend on other people. Virgo across the axis brings romance, creativity, children, pleasure, and your own desire back into the calculation.

You may leave a group, become more visible inside one, change a collaboration, or realize that a goal you once wanted now requires a version of your life you do not actually want. A larger circle is not useful if maintaining your place in it consumes the time you wanted the connections to make possible. Pay attention to the people who still make sense when there is no invitation, introduction, audience, or opportunity attached. The future is allowed to change when you learn more about what you want your days to contain.

Something you have been carrying privately may be ready to end, or at least stop running your days from the background. A lunar eclipse in Pisces lands in your 12th house, bringing a culmination around endings, solitude, grief, recovery, private work, and the parts of your life that become easier to hear when there is less noise around them. Virgo across the axis makes the practical cost visible through work, routines, appointments, health, and the daily tasks that still have to happen.

You may finish a private chapter, step away from an obligation nobody knew was taking so much from you, or realize that exhaustion has been shaping decisions you thought were about something else. The point is not to disappear from your life. It is to stop treating rest and recovery as whatever is left after every other responsibility has been handled. Close what is actually over. Protect the time needed to recover from what is not.

The next chapter may depend less on having a new idea than changing the structure that decides what can happen. A New Moon in Aquarius begins a cycle around friendships, communities, systems, technology, shared goals, and the future you are trying to build with other people. Aquarius is fixed air ruled traditionally by Saturn, so the useful beginning is not only imaginative. It needs a framework strong enough to keep the idea moving after the first burst of enthusiasm.

A collaboration may need clearer roles, a group may need a better way to make decisions, or a new tool or process may make an old goal possible in a different way. Do not mistake being unconventional for automatically being right. The strongest change solves a problem you can name and still works once other people have to use it. Choose one future-facing improvement you can actually support with time, responsibility, and follow-through. The experiment becomes valuable when it changes what is possible in ordinary life.
